verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.173
verses.english: Numbered Discourses 4.173

verses.pali: 18. Sañcetaniyavagga
verses.english: 18. Intention

verses.pali: Mahākoṭṭhikasutta
verses.english: With Mahākoṭṭhita

verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmā mahākoṭṭhiko yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sāriputtena saddhiṁ sammodi.
verses.english: Then Venerable Mahākoṭṭhita went up to Venerable Sāriputta, and exchanged greetings with him.

verses.pali: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā mahākoṭṭhiko āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, Mahākoṭṭhita sat down to one side, and said to Sāriputta:

verses.pali: “Channaṁ, āvuso, phassāyatanānaṁ asesavirāganirodhā atthaññaṁ kiñcī”ti?
verses.english: “Reverend, when the six fields of contact have faded away and ceased with no residue left behind, does something else still exist?”

verses.pali: “Mā hevaṁ, āvuso”.
verses.english: “Don’t put it like that, reverend.”

verses.pali: “Channaṁ, āvuso, phassāyatanānaṁ asesavirāganirodhā natthaññaṁ kiñcī”ti?
verses.english: “Does something else no longer exist?”

verses.pali: “Mā hevaṁ, āvuso”.
verses.english: “Don’t put it like that, reverend.”

verses.pali: “Channaṁ, āvuso, phassāyatanānaṁ asesavirāganirodhā atthi ca natthi ca aññaṁ kiñcī”ti?
verses.english: “Does something else both still exist and no longer exist?”

verses.pali: “Mā hevaṁ, āvuso”.
verses.english: “Don’t put it like that, reverend.”

verses.pali: “Channaṁ, āvuso, phassāyatanānaṁ asesavirāganirodhā nevatthi no natthaññaṁ kiñcī”ti?
verses.english: “Does something else neither still exist nor no longer exist?”

verses.pali: “Mā hevaṁ, āvuso”.
verses.english: “Don’t put it like that, reverend.”

verses.pali: “‘Channaṁ, āvuso, phassāyatanānaṁ asesavirāganirodhā atthaññaṁ kiñcī’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno ‘mā hevaṁ, āvuso’ti vadesi.
verses.english: “Reverend, when asked whether—when the six fields of contact have faded away and ceased with no residue left behind—something else still exists, you say ‘don’t put it like that’.

verses.pali: ‘Channaṁ, āvuso, phassāyatanānaṁ asesavirāganirodhā natthaññaṁ kiñcī’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno:
verses.english: When asked whether something else no longer exists,

verses.pali: ‘mā hevaṁ, āvuso’ti vadesi.
verses.english: you say ‘don’t put it like that’.

verses.pali: ‘Channaṁ, āvuso, phassāyatanānaṁ asesavirāganirodhā atthi ca natthi ca aññaṁ kiñcī’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno:
verses.english: When asked whether something else both still exists and no longer exists,

verses.pali: ‘mā hevaṁ, āvuso’ti vadesi.
verses.english: you say ‘don’t put it like that’.

verses.pali: ‘Channaṁ, āvuso, phassāyatanānaṁ asesavirāganirodhā nevatthi no natthaññaṁ kiñcī’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno:
verses.english: When asked whether something else neither still exists nor no longer exists,

verses.pali: ‘mā hevaṁ, āvuso’ti vadesi.
verses.english: you say ‘don’t put it like that’.

verses.pali: Yathā kathaṁ pana, āvuso, imassa bhāsitassa attho daṭṭhabbo”ti?
verses.english: How then should we see the meaning of this statement?”

verses.pali: “‘Channaṁ, āvuso, phassāyatanānaṁ asesavirāganirodhā atthaññaṁ kiñcī’ti, iti vadaṁ appapañcaṁ papañceti.
verses.english: “In saying that, ‘When the six fields of contact have faded away and ceased with no residue left behind, something else still exists’, you’re proliferating the unproliferated.

verses.pali: ‘Channaṁ, āvuso, phassāyatanānaṁ asesavirāganirodhā natthaññaṁ kiñcī’ti, iti vadaṁ appapañcaṁ papañceti.
verses.english: In saying that, ‘something else no longer exists’, you’re proliferating the unproliferated.

verses.pali: ‘Channaṁ, āvuso, phassāyatanānaṁ asesavirāganirodhā atthi ca natthi ca aññaṁ kiñcī’ti, iti vadaṁ appapañcaṁ papañceti.
verses.english: In saying that, ‘something else both still exists and no longer exists’, you’re proliferating the unproliferated.

verses.pali: ‘Channaṁ, āvuso, phassāyatanānaṁ asesavirāganirodhā nevatthi no natthaññaṁ kiñcī’ti, iti vadaṁ appapañcaṁ papañceti.
verses.english: In saying that, ‘something else neither still exists nor no longer exists’, you’re proliferating the unproliferated.

verses.pali: Yāvatā, āvuso, channaṁ phassāyatanānaṁ gati tāvatā papañcassa gati;
verses.english: The scope of proliferation extends as far as the scope of the six fields of contact.

verses.pali: yāvatā papañcassa gati tāvatā channaṁ phassāyatanānaṁ gati.
verses.english: The scope of the six fields of contact extends as far as the scope of proliferation.

verses.pali: Channaṁ, āvuso, phassāyatanānaṁ asesavirāganirodhā papañcanirodho papañcavūpasamo”ti.
verses.english: When the six fields of contact fade away and cease with no residue left behind, proliferation stops and is stilled.”

verses.pali: Tatiyaṁ.
